from.place: ## Proof: passage from the Cech cohomology of [lem-pc-cech-computes] (all index tuples) to the alternating Cech complex indexed by subsets

title: The alternating Cech complex computes Cech cohomology
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal U:X=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ be an open covering, viewed as a covering of the Zariski site of $X$ [def-sc-zariski-site], with Cech complex $\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ and Cech cohomology $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex] for a presheaf of abelian groups $\mathcal F$ on $X$. Choose a total order $<$ on $I$ and write $U_{i_0\dots i_p}=U_{i_0}\cap\dots\cap U_{i_p}$. The *alternating (ordered) Cech complex* $\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet_{\mathrm{alt}}(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ has $\check{\mathcal C}^p_{\mathrm{alt}}(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)=\prod_{i_0<\dots<i_p}\mathcal F(U_{i_0\dots i_p})$ for $p\ge0$, zero for $p<0$, and differential $d(s)_{i_0\dots i_{p+1}}=\sum_{j=0}^{p+1}(-1)^j\,s_{i_0\dots\hat{i_j}\dots i_{p+1}}|_{U_{i_0\dots i_{p+1}}}$. Then restricting a cochain to the strictly increasing index tuples is a cochain map $\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)\to\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet_{\mathrm{alt}}(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$, and it induces isomorphisms $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)\cong H^p(\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet_{\mathrm{alt}}(\mathcal U,\mathcal F))$ for all $p\ge0$.

source.place: Cohomology of Sheaves, Section 20.23 (Cech cohomology: the alternating and ordered Cech complexes), the lemma that the ordered Cech complex is homotopy equivalent to the full Cech complex
